summary: Sustained short-window 429s after switching to pooled-proxy signed-url strategy during large multipart embedding import
description:
Issue summary:
Customer LexiData reports steady stream of 429 responses for an otherwise healthy multipart embedding import that started after they switched to a pooled-proxy + short-lived signed URL callback flow. The errors are concentrated during concurrent callback fanout and appear as sustained short-window throttles (soft 429s) rather than a single burst.

Impact:
- Production embedding backfill stalled for multiple jobs, causing downstream search freshness degradation for LexiData customers.
- Errors began ~2026-03-09 18:10 UTC and persist intermittently across the affected import windows.

User-reported context:
- They moved from direct single-host uploads to a pooled proxy (customer-side) that multiplexes callbacks to our signed-url endpoint.
- Each signed URL rotation results in ~50 short-lived callbacks at once.
- Happens only in us-east region and only for multipart embedding imports, normal single-record embedding calls unaffected.
steps_to_reproduce:
1) Create a multipart embedding import job with ~20k records. 2) Configure client to obtain signed URLs and fan out upload confirmations via a pooled proxy that reuses a small outbound IP NAT pool. 3) Trigger parallel uploads so callbacks hit our /signed-url/confirm endpoint concurrently. 4) Observe 429s returned on confirm and subsequent embedding finalize calls.

Observed behavior: 429s are returned with X-RateLimit-* headers indicating short-window token exhaustion; headers show per-route window exhausted despite tenant-level credits remaining.
logs:
[2026-03-09T18:12:03Z] svc=api-gateway route=/signed-url/confirm key=lexidata-acc token_window=short_window remaining=0 status=429 src_ip=52.18.34.21 nat_pool_id=np-03
[2026-03-09T18:12:04Z] svc=rate-limiter tenant=lexidata credits_global=1200 credits_route=0 window_ms=250 status=throttled
[trace] request_id=abc123 callback_batch=37 concurrent=42
comments: 2026-03-10 - Ava Chen (Support): Logged issue after customer provided request traces and timing samples. Noticed correlation with NAT pool reuse based on src_ip clusters.

2026-03-10 - Diego Ramos (SRE): Confirmed X-RateLimit-Window values show short (250ms) windows hitting zero. Tentative hypothesis: per-route token accounting plus proxy IP fanout causing double-counting across many callbacks that share src IPs.

2026-03-11 - LexiData (Customer): We can provision a separate IP pool on our side but would prefer guidance on server-side config changes first. Adding metrics and a link to our upload proxy logs: https://logs.lexidata.com/ingest/2026-03-09

2026-03-12 - Diego Ramos (SRE): Deployed temporary route-isolation flag for lexidata signed-url path to reduce per-route coupling. Saw immediate reduction in 429 rate by ~70% in next window. Will keep in place while engineering works on fix.
investigation_notes:
Hypotheses considered:
- NAT/proxy IP reuse results in our edge layer attributing many callbacks to a single source, exhausting per-connection/per-route short-window token buckets.
- Signed-url rotation pattern triggers burst of small requests that are counted against route-level windows rather than being attributed to the originating API key because of how proxy reuses IP and strips API-key metadata.
Evidence:
- src_ip clustering in gateway logs (same nat_pool_id across many requests).
- X-RateLimit headers show route window exhaustion while tenant_global credits remain >500.
- Enabling route isolation for the signed-url path reduced 429s by 70% in immediate sample.
Next steps:
- Recommend engineering implement per-origin-key weighting on the route to avoid penalizing tenants who use small NAT pools.
- Add a separate short-window burst pool for signed-url confirm paths or mark confirms as low-cost control messages not counted toward the same route quota as tokenized generation/embedding calls.
- Product/Docs: recommend guidance to customers to avoid small NAT pools or to add jitter and backoff on callback fanout.
resolution:
Workaround applied: route-isolation flag enabled for /signed-url/confirm for LexiData which reduced 429s by ~70%; advised customer to increase client-side jitter and rotate through larger outbound IP pool.
Engineering fix (in progress): engineering ticket created to add 'control' cost-class for signed-url confirms and to implement per-origin attribution in rate-limiter so that callbacks forwarded via pooled proxies don't double-count for route windows.
Follow-up: SRE to monitor for 48 hours and then SRE+ENG to roll changes to staging and then prod. Customer to confirm ingestion success after incremental retry window.
resolution_notes: Temporary mitigation is in place; change will remain until PR merges and rollouts complete. Customer agreed to postpone immediate migration until fix lands to avoid disrupting traffic patterns.
follow_up_actions: ENG-12456: implement per-origin attribution in rate-limiter (owner: Diego Ramos)
DOCS-987: add signed-url callback best-practices to support docs
SRE-1301: monitor lexidata signed-url route for 48h post-change
customer_communication:
2026-03-10: Acknowledged and asked for traces (Support -> LexiData).
2026-03-11: Provided workaround and recommended changes to client proxy (Support -> LexiData).
2026-03-12: Confirmed temporary route-isolation reduced errors; engineering working on permanent fix. Next update expected 2026-03-15.
notes_for_engineering:
- Consider adding a low-cost control path for signed-url confirms that does not draw from generation/embedding route windows.
- Evaluate per-src-ip vs per-api-key attribution tradeoffs; prefer api-key attribution when present to avoid pooled-proxy fanout issues.
- Add integration test simulating NAT pool reuse and bursty callbacks to prevent regression.
- Include a flag to allow customers on enterprise tier to opt into dedicated burst pool for callback-heavy workflows.
